findings.body:
Empty or whitespace-only `user.name` makes this crash: `"".split()` and `"   ".split()` both return `[]`, so `[0]` raises `IndexError`. Guard the split result (or reject blank names explicitly) before indexing.

```suggestion
def first_name(user):
    parts = user.name.split()
    return parts[0] if parts else ""
```

summary:
## Verdict

Small utility tweak with one real edge-case bug in the new helper.

## Notes

`total()` now short-circuits on falsy `items` and returns `0`. For an empty list that matches what `sum(...)` already does; the guard is still useful when `items` is `None`, where the old code raised `TypeError`.

`first_name()` is new and crashes on empty or whitespace-only `user.name` because `"".split()` / `"   ".split()` yield `[]` and `[0]` raises `IndexError`. Same call also assumes `user` and `user.name` are present and string-typed.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: `first_name` does `user.name.split()[0]` with no guard; `"".split()` and whitespace-only splits are `[]`, so indexing raises `IndexError`. Warning severity is appropriate for this correctness bug.
